title: Design System: Montreal Secondary Open Days

display-band.purpose: School name set on its region lobe.

motion.name: ease-overshoot
motion.purpose: The world's one motion grammar: transforms on pins, buttons, capsules, chevrons.

motion.name: move
motion.purpose: Duration for every transition; colour/fill changes use plain ease.

narrative.overview:
The page is water. Greater Montreal is drawn as the archipelago it actually is, from OSM geometry rendered as a self-drawn SVG: flat, unmodulated land lobes, one colour per region, separated by cream rivers. Schools live on that land. The map is not an illustration bolted onto a directory; it *is* the region filter, and every other surface (rows, swatches, counts, the school page band) inherits its colour by region.

Everything around the map is quiet and ink-drawn: one grotesk family set tight and heavy for titles, hairline sand rules between rows, and capsule controls outlined in ink at 1.5px. Colour is spent almost entirely on land. Coral is the only alarm in the system and it is rationed to what a parent must not miss: entrance exams, clashes, and the school pin. Motion has one voice, a 0.4s overshoot, so selecting a region feels like the land swelling into place rather than a tab switching.

Gaps are shown as gaps. A school renders only what is confirmed: an unknown language or student body leaves its cap out, a missing description says so, never filler.
keyCharacteristics: Cream water ground; flat colour land per region; no gradients, no texture on land.
The map is the region filter; region capsules mirror it as the accessible control.
Capsule-shaped everything interactive, 1.5px ink outlines, no shadows.
One family (Bricolage Grotesque, optical size axis) for display and body.
Coral rationed to entrance exams, clashes and the map pin.
One motion grammar: 0.4s with a single overshoot.

rules.name: The Land Is Identity Rule
rules.body: The four land colours mean "this region". Don't use them as decoration, status or category colour.

rules.name: The Island Action Rule
rules.body: The one sanctioned exception: island green fills the primary button and the active nav capsule. No other land colour does action work.

rules.name: The Coral Ration Rule
rules.body: Coral marks only entrance exams, clashes and the map pin. If something else turns coral, the alarm stops meaning anything.

rules.name: The Cream-Only Secondary Ink Rule
rules.body: Secondary ink is legal only on cream grounds (`water-cream`, `water-shade`, the coral wash). It fails contrast on land colours; text on land is always full ink.

rules.name: The Two-Step Weight Rule
rules.body: h1 and h2 sit at 700 with -0.03em tracking; h3 and list headings drop to 600 so long lists scan. Interface labels are 500. Never synthesize weights (`font-synthesis: none`).

rules.name: The Flat Land Rule
rules.body: Land and surfaces are flat colour. No drop shadows, no gradients, no relief shading on lobes.

dos: **Do** route all motion through the overshoot easing (`cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)`) at 0.4s for transforms; colour and fill changes use plain ease at the same 0.4s.
**Do** set region colour through `data-region` so lobes, swatches, counts and bands stay in sync.
**Do** make every interactive control a capsule with a 1.5px outline: sand at rest, ink when active.
**Do** put full ink, never secondary ink, on any land colour.
**Do** show missing data as an honest gap in secondary ink.
donts: **Don't** use coral for anything but entrance exams, clashes and the map pin.
**Don't** use land colours for non-region meaning; island green's button/nav role is the only exception.
**Don't** add shadows, gradients or texture to land or surfaces.
**Don't** bring in map tiles or a third-party map widget; the archipelago is self-drawn from OSM geometry.
**Don't** add a second typeface; Bricolage Grotesque's optical sizes cover display and text.
